Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with longitudinal chromatin accessibility tracking
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or wounding-like signals), then run ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at multiple time points, including long after the stimulus is gone. Sites that stay open and AP-1 bound after the signal clears, and that give a faster or stronger response on restimulation, would indicate a memory function.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at defined windows (degron)
ideas.description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degradation of FOS, JUN, or a dominant-negative such as A-FOS, and deplete AP-1 either during the priming stimulus or only after it, during the memory period. If depletion during priming blocks later enhanced responses but depletion during the memory period does not, AP-1 is needed to establish the memory. If depletion during the memory period also erases it, AP-1 is needed to maintain it.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage/clonal tracking
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq on primed and naive populations, with barcoded lineages, to relate AP-1 motif accessibility to transcriptional output across cell divisions. This tests whether the primed state is heritable through mitosis in clonal sisters and whether it depends on AP-1 motif activity.

ideas.title: Enhancer mutagenesis and CRISPR perturbation of AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Use CRISPRi/dCas9 or base editing to disrupt specific AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers. Then measure whether the primed accessibility, histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1), and the enhanced re-induction of nearby genes are lost. Reporter or endogenous readouts would show whether the sites are causal rather than merely correlated.

ideas.title: Live-cell AP-1 dynamics and optogenetic priming
ideas.description: Track AP-1 activity in single cells with live reporters or imaging of FOS/JUN levels and binding. Combine this with optogenetic or pulsatile stimulation using different durations and frequencies, then record later responses. This shows whether the dose, duration, and history of AP-1 activity predict the strength of a later response, and whether the memory is stored in the cell state or in ongoing AP-1 signaling.
